name: Shontel M. Brown

data_centers.summary: Brown has signed on to two House bills that would make data centers pay their own grid costs so families' electric bills do not rise, and she voted against Republican grid-expansion bills. She has not made her own public statements about data centers as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6529, Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (Landsman)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs the leading House Democratic bill to keep the cost of power lines and plants built for AI data centers off household electric bills.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7977, Energy Bills Relief Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined a Democratic package aimed at high energy bills that includes making data centers cover their own costs; cosponsorship date confirmed on govtrack.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 1047, GRID Power Act (passed House 216-206)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against a Republican bill to fast-track gas and other dispatchable power plants that its sponsor tied to central Ohio data center demand.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 3616, Reliable Power Act (passed House 225-203)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against a second Republican grid bill framed around meeting rising power demand.

ai_risk.summary: Brown wants specific rules on AI harms: she wrote the 2024 bill banning AI deepfakes that trick voters, pressed the FEC and DOJ on election deepfakes, and cosponsors bills requiring bias testing of automated systems and an AI civil rights law. She also backs AI training and hiring in government, so she is not anti-AI.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 8858 (118th), Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill would ban using AI fakes to deceive voters and require disclaimers on AI-generated election content, enforced by the FTC.

evidence.title: Press release: Congresswoman Brown Introduces Legislation to Protect Elections from AI Deception
evidence.quote: Deceptive AI-generated content is a threat to elections, voters, and our democracy. AI-generated content is a powerful new tool requiring oversight and regulation to ensure our elections are secure, and the rights of voters are protected.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words, AI content needs oversight and regulation to protect voters.

evidence.title: Letter to FEC urging it to treat AI deepfakes as fraudulent misrepresentation
evidence.quote: AI has the potential to supercharge deception in an ecosystem already rife with false content
evidence.what_it_shows: Led a letter asking the FEC to apply existing fraud law to AI deepfakes in campaign ads after the Grok-2 release.

evidence.title: Brown-Sewell bipartisan letter to DOJ, DHS and EAC on AI interference in the 2024 election (33 signers)
evidence.quote: AI generated misinformation aimed at voter suppression isn't a theory, it's already happening
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked federal agencies for a plan to counter AI-driven voter intimidation and misinformation, especially targeting Black voters.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5511, Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring companies to test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report to the FTC.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6356, Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning discriminatory AI and requiring companies to audit their systems before and after use.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4894, Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making it illegal to spread lies about voting, including AI-made fakes, before federal elections.

evidence.title: Letter to DHS Secretary Noem on ICE mass cellphone-location surveillance tools (12 signers)
evidence.quote: Mass location tracking without a warrant should alarm every American, regardless of party.
evidence.what_it_shows: Led Oversight Democrats demanding legal authority and privacy safeguards for government surveillance technology.

evidence.title: Press release: Brown co-leads the AI Training Extension Act with Rep. Mace
evidence.quote: I'm proud to co-lead this bipartisan bill to expand AI training across the federal workforce.
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports government adopting AI, with training that covers risks, privacy and cybersecurity.

evidence.title: Press release (Rep. Jacobs): bipartisan AI Talent Act introduced with Brown as a House co-lead
evidence.quote: I am proud to co-lead this bipartisan bill that will help ensure AI is used responsibly throughout government and strengthen U.S. leadership in the technologies of the future
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames responsible government AI use and U.S. leadership as compatible goals.

tech_regulation.summary: Brown pushes targeted privacy and security rules: she demanded probes of DOGE data handling and airline passenger privacy, questioned ICE surveillance tools, and backed forcing TikTok's sale and banning China-linked connected cars. She has not called for breaking up Big Tech or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Brown and Sen. Wyden letter asking GAO to investigate DOT's failure to enforce airline passenger privacy
evidence.quote: DOT's abdication of its role as a privacy regulator has left the sensitive personal information of hundreds of millions of Americans exposed to corporate exploitation, warrantless government surveillance, and warrantless seizure of money and other property
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants regulators to actively enforce consumer data privacy.

evidence.title: Brown, Trahan, DelBene letter to Treasury and GSA inspectors general on DOGE privacy violations
evidence.quote: Such an investigation is especially imperative as we determine the extent to which federal privacy laws were violated and how individual Americans were adversely affected
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats the Privacy Act as a hard limit on how government handles personal data.

evidence.title: Statement on TikTok ahead of the divest-or-ban deadline
evidence.quote: Congress intended to sever TikTok's ties to foreign adversaries, not ban it outright. I believe TikTok should remain available to Americans, just under new ownership.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports forced divestiture on data-security grounds but not an outright ban.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7521 (118th), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the law forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car technology from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3420 (118th), My Body, My Data Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports limits on apps collecting and sharing reproductive health data.

preemption.summary: Brown signed the Nov. 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats telling congressional leaders not to revive the ban on state AI laws in the defense bill or through an executive order. She has not issued her own statement on the issue.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order (Brown is a signer)
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: She put her name on a clear statement that states should keep enforcing their own AI laws.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 1 (reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year state AI law moratorium)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against the package containing the moratorium, though the vote covered the whole reconciliation bill.

china_chips.summary: Brown sits on the House Select Committee on China and cosponsors bills removing Chinese AI app DeepSeek from government devices and banning China-linked connected cars. No statements found on Nvidia chip sales or export controls specifically.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 1121, No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports keeping the Chinese AI model DeepSeek off federal computers and phones.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports barring Chinese-tied car software and hardware from the U.S. market, a China-hawk technology stance.

signature: Wrote the 2024 Securing Elections From AI Deception Act and led letters pressing regulators on AI deepfakes and ICE surveillance tech; top Democrat on the Oversight cybersecurity and IT subcommittee.

notable_quote.text: Deceptive AI-generated content is a threat to elections, voters, and our democracy. AI-generated content is a powerful new tool requiring oversight and regulation to ensure our elections are secure, and the rights of voters are protected.

groups: Ranking Member, House Oversight Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation
search_notes: Ran about 12 Google News searches (AI, data centers, electricity bills, deepfakes, Big Tech/privacy, China chips, preemption, surveillance, Select Committee) plus a site listing of shontelbrown.house.gov. Fetched and read 9 official press releases, the Jacobs AI Talent Act release, govtrack roll calls h145/h279/h347 and cosponsor pages for H.R. 6529 and H.R. 7977, and extracted the Matsui letter PDF to confirm her signature. She did not sign the Dec. 3, 2025 Clarke letter. Cleveland.com and Reuters pages were blocked (403) and Wayback was refusing connections, so the ICE surveillance story and airline privacy story were read from her own releases instead. No data center statement in her own words was found. The Oct. 2025 Paragon spyware letter was referenced but not fetched.

name: Troy Balderson

data_centers.summary: Balderson is proud that central Ohio is a national data center hub and has written three bills to add power plants and plan the grid for the boom, but he says data centers must find their own power and not put costs on his constituents. He has not joined the committee's main Ratepayer Protection Act.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 1047, GRID Power Act (passed House 216-206 on Sept. 18, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill lets grid operators fast-track gas and other dispatchable power plants through the interconnection queue to meet rising demand.

evidence.title: Press release: Balderson's Bill to Lower Energy Costs and Improve Grid Reliability Passes House
evidence.quote: These facilities are powering the American AI revolution, but we must ensure we can keep them running while also providing reliable, affordable energy to Ohio families.
evidence.what_it_shows: Casts data centers as a positive to keep running, paired with a promise of affordable power for families.

evidence.title: Energy and Commerce full committee hearing on AI and American Global Competitiveness (Balderson questions Eric Schmidt)
evidence.quote: I'm proud to represent one of the largest clusters of data centers in the country. Google, Amazon Web Services, Meta, QTS, Vantage, and more have data centers in central Ohio and my district.
evidence.what_it_shows: Celebrates the buildout and asks how tech companies should help bring new generation online.

evidence.title: Remarks at Zanesville-Muskingum County Chamber legislative breakfast (WHIZ News)
evidence.quote: These data centers are going to have to find their own power source. We cannot put that on the backs of our constituents.
evidence.what_it_shows: His clearest condition: data centers should self-supply power rather than shift costs to residents.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 9332, Load Forecasting Enhancement Act (approved by Energy and Commerce 47-0 on July 21, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Aims to stop utilities from overbuilding for speculative data center projects that would raise ratepayer costs.

evidence.title: Press release: House Committee Approves Balderson Bill to Strengthen Grid and Protect Ratepayers
evidence.quote: By giving states and utilities the tools they need, we can ensure we expand and improve our grid as efficiently as possible
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames grid expansion as the goal, with better forecasting as the ratepayer safeguard.

evidence.title: Joint press release with Rep. Menendez on the Load Forecasting Enhancement Act advancing in subcommittee
evidence.quote: This bipartisan bill will help states and utilities make better decisions, plan for future demand, and avoid passing unnecessary costs on to consumers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Works across the aisle on consumer cost protection while keeping the grid growing.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 3616, Reliable Power Act (passed House 225-203 on Dec. 17, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires federal agencies to weigh grid reliability before finalizing rules, a pro-generation measure critics called a gift to polluters.

evidence.title: Press release: Balderson, Cotton Introduce CLEAR Act to limit lawsuits against energy projects
evidence.quote: To unleash American energy, lower costs, and strengthen our energy security, we must restore predictability and common sense to our permitting system.
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants energy infrastructure built faster with fewer legal delays.

evidence.title: Govtrack cosponsor list for H.R. 9340, Ratepayer Protection Act (Balderson listed as not a cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Despite sitting on the Energy Subcommittee, he has not signed on to the committee's flagship bill making 100 MW-plus loads pay full incremental costs.

ai_risk.summary: No public position found on AI safety rules, chatbots, deepfakes or AI liability as of Sept 2026. His AI remarks focus on powering data centers and winning the AI race, not on regulating the technology.

evidence.title: Energy and Commerce hearing on AI and American Global Competitiveness (Balderson questions)
evidence.what_it_shows: His only AI hearing appearance found used the time to ask about power supply for data centers, not about AI rules.

tech_regulation.summary: Balderson is one of nine members of the House Republican working group drafting a national data privacy law and cosponsors a ban on China-linked connected-car technology. No statements found on Section 230, antitrust or kids' online safety.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: House Republicans form Energy and Commerce data privacy working group; Balderson named as a member
evidence.what_it_shows: He is helping write a comprehensive federal privacy standard, a targeted rule for tech companies.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car software and parts from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

preemption.summary: No statement found on whether Washington should override state AI laws. He voted for the May 2025 reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year moratorium, but that vote covered hundreds of unrelated provisions and is not treated as a position here.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1 (reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year state AI law moratorium)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported the package that included the moratorium; the vote alone does not show his view on preemption.

china_chips.summary: Balderson led Ohio Republicans in 2022 urging full funding of the CHIPS Act for Intel's Ohio plant, which is about building chips at home. No position found on export controls or Nvidia chip sales to China.

evidence.title: Ohio Republican letter to congressional leaders urging full funding of the CHIPS for America Act (led by Balderson; reported in Carey release)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports domestic chip manufacturing subsidies, not a stance on chip exports to China.

signature: Energy and Commerce member and House Energy Action Team chair who wrote the GRID Power, Reliable Power and Load Forecasting Acts to power central Ohio's data center boom while insisting data centers find their own power.

notable_quote.text: These data centers are going to have to find their own power source. We cannot put that on the backs of our constituents.

groups: Vice Chairman, House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations
Member, House Energy and Commerce Republican Data Privacy Working Group
search_notes: Ran about 12 Google News searches (AI, data centers, electricity/grid, chatbots/deepfakes, Big Tech/privacy, China chips, preemption, Energy Action Team, Intel/New Albany, energy summit, challenger). Site listing of balderson.house.gov returned little, so I pulled the press release index directly and read releases 2887, 2994, 2859, 2744, 2748, 2905 and 2918 (2918, the Reliable Power Act passage release, displayed the wrong body text on the site). Read the Menendez joint release, WHIZ Zanesville story, E&C AI hearing recap, E&C FERC hearing recap, MeriTalk privacy group story, govtrack pages for H.R. 1047, 3616, 9332 and 9340 and roll calls h145/h279/h347. Politico (Apr 30 and Sept 6, 2026), Daily Energy Insider, Punchbowl and the Nov. 2024 Cleveland.com op-ed were blocked and Wayback refused connections. No AI regulation or preemption statements found.

name: Emilia Strong Sykes

data_centers.summary: As top Democrat on the Science Committee's oversight panel, Sykes says data centers can bring jobs but communities need strong guardrails on electricity costs, environment and health, and she rejects the Trump administration's rapid-expansion approach. She cosponsors two bills to keep data center costs off family electric bills.

evidence.title: Ranking member remarks at Science oversight subcommittee hearing on data center infrastructure (reported by Roll Call)
evidence.quote: We must fully understand the trade-offs of data centers, both the potential they hold for quality jobs and investment in our communities, and the impact on electricity costs, our environment and even our health
evidence.what_it_shows: Balances investment in her district against cost, environmental and health worries.

evidence.title: Ranking member remarks at Science oversight subcommittee hearing on data center infrastructure (reported by Roll Call)
evidence.quote: One path is the Trump administration's approach: few safeguards, rapid expansion and a total embrace of data centers with little thought to the communities that host them
evidence.what_it_shows: Explicitly rejects a build-fast approach and calls for strong guardrails for host communities.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7066, SHIELD Act (data center electric bill protections)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping families from being stuck with higher bills caused by power-hungry data centers; date confirmed on govtrack.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7977, Energy Bills Relief Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined the Democratic energy-bill package that makes data centers pay their own costs; date confirmed on govtrack.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 1047, GRID Power Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed the Republican bill fast-tracking dispatchable power plants tied to data center demand.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 3616, Reliable Power Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed a second Republican grid bill framed around rising power demand.

ai_risk.summary: Sykes cosponsored the 2024 bill banning AI deepfakes that deceive voters, but most of her AI work is about helping small manufacturers and workers use AI. The AI industry super PAC Think Big endorsed her without spending money. No statement found on broader AI safety rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8858 (118th), Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning AI fakes used to trick voters, a targeted guardrail.

evidence.title: Press release: Science Committee passes Sykes amendment to help small manufacturers use AI
evidence.quote: Expanding support for these programs will ensure more small businesses and manufacturers have the training and services they need to implement cutting-edge artificial intelligence technologies in their practices
evidence.what_it_shows: Her AI focus is adoption and workforce help, not restrictions.

evidence.title: Legis1: Science Committee advanced 10 AI bills in late June 2026 with a Sykes workforce amendment adopted
evidence.what_it_shows: Continues to shape AI bills around worker impacts rather than safety mandates.

evidence.title: The New Republic: Think Big (Leading the Future's Democratic arm) endorsed Sykes without financial support
evidence.quote: Think Big has also offered endorsements (but not financial support) to Sam Liccardo, Josh Gottheimer, Jimmy Gomez, Tom Suozzi, Eric Sorensen, Joyce Beatty, Herb Conaway, Emilia Sykes, and Suhas Subramanyam.
evidence.what_it_shows: The industry-aligned super PAC that fights state AI regulation views her as friendly, though it gave her no money.

tech_regulation.summary: Sykes voted to force TikTok's sale and said all social media apps should be safely regulated for privacy, backed a bill to keep unvetted DOGE staff out of Treasury data, and cosponsors bills on connected-car data and China-linked car technology. No calls for breaking up Big Tech found.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Sykes votes for the TikTok divest-or-ban bill (H.R. 7521)
evidence.quote: I believe there is more work to be done to ensure all social media apps, not just TikTok, can be safely regulated to protect the privacy and security of all Americans who use them.
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants privacy and security regulation across social media, not just TikTok.

evidence.title: Press release: Sykes joins Taxpayer Data Protection Act to stop Musk's DOGE team accessing Treasury systems
evidence.quote: prevent Musk and his minions from rifling through the private data of everyday Americans
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats access to Americans' personal data as something that needs legal limits.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 2110, Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring carmakers to cut off abusers' remote access to a survivor's car data.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car technology from companies tied to China and other adversaries.

preemption.summary: Sykes signed the Nov. 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats opposing any revival of the state AI law moratorium in the defense bill or through an executive order. She has not issued her own statement on preemption.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order (Sykes is a signer)
evidence.quote: We strongly support innovation, and it is simply wrong to accept the premise that identifying and addressing AI-specific risks, and setting common-sense guardrails, is incompatible with U.S. leadership in AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed on to the position that states should keep enforcing their own AI laws absent federal protections.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 1 (reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year state AI law moratorium)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against the package containing the moratorium, though the vote covered the whole bill.

china_chips.summary: Sykes is a strong defender of the CHIPS and Science Act and Intel's Ohio plant and cosponsored a bill to speed chip factory construction, which is about building chips at home. No position found on export controls or Nvidia chip sales to China.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Sykes rejects Trump's claim that the CHIPS Act is horrible
evidence.quote: Repealing the CHIPS and Science Act would have a direct negative impact on Ohio's 13th district and I will stand in the way of anyone who attempts to undermine our local economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: Defends domestic chip and tech-hub subsidies; says nothing about chip exports.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4549 (118th), Building Chips in America Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported letting new chip factories skip some environmental reviews to get built faster.

signature: Top Democrat on the Science Committee's oversight panel who calls for strong guardrails for communities hosting data centers and backs bills to keep data center costs off electric bills; endorsed without money by the AI industry PAC Think Big.

notable_quote.text: One path is the Trump administration's approach: few safeguards, rapid expansion and a total embrace of data centers with little thought to the communities that host them

groups: Ranking Member, House Science, Space, and Technology Subcommittee on Investigations and Oversight
search_notes: Ran about 13 Google News searches (AI, data centers, electricity bills, deepfakes/chatbots, Big Tech/privacy, CHIPS, preemption, SHIELD/Energy Bills Relief, Science hearings, Think Big, WARN Act/AI layoffs, Akron press). Site listing of sykes.house.gov (42 URLs) and fetched 9 official releases, the Roll Call hearing story in full, the Science Democrats hearing page and ranking-member announcement, Legis1, PBS and The New Republic PAC piece. Confirmed her signature in the Matsui letter PDF; she did not sign the Clarke letter. Confirmed H.R. 7066 and H.R. 7977 cosponsorship dates on govtrack and votes h145/h279/h347. Her official Feb. 24, 2026 opening statement PDF could not be downloaded (site served an HTML redirect), so the Roll Call transcript quotes are used. Cleveland.com and Bloomberg Law pages were blocked.

name: David P. Joyce

data_centers.summary: No public statements on data centers, electric bills or the Ohio buildout were found as of Sept 2026. He voted with his party for two Republican grid-expansion bills, which by themselves do not show a data center position.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1047, GRID Power Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported fast-tracking dispatchable power plants; sponsors cited data center demand, but the vote was party-line.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 3616, Reliable Power Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported a second Republican grid bill framed around rising power demand.

ai_risk.summary: Joyce, who oversees FTC funding, told the agency regulators should keep common-sense guardrails without stifling AI innovation, while also pressing for resources to enforce the Take It Down Act. He cosponsors the DEFIANCE Act letting deepfake porn victims sue. Mixed, light-touch-leaning record.

evidence.title: Chairman Joyce opening remarks at Appropriations oversight hearing on the Federal Trade Commission
evidence.quote: While regulators have a responsibility to maintain common-sense guardrails, they should do so in a way that does not stifle innovation and force good-paying jobs overseas
evidence.what_it_shows: Accepts some AI guardrails but frames them around not slowing innovation.

evidence.title: Chairman Joyce opening remarks at Appropriations oversight hearing on the Federal Trade Commission
evidence.quote: the recent passage of the Take It Down Act will require the FTC to deploy additional resources to crack down on the publication of non-consensual intimate images, including those generated by AI
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports funding enforcement of the new federal law against AI-generated intimate images.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue people who make or share AI sexual deepfakes of them.

tech_regulation.summary: Joyce backs targeted rules on dating-app scams, deepfake porn and (in 2021) Big Tech content moderation transparency, but as FTC and FCC appropriator he praised the FTC for pulling back from its earlier aggressive course and moved to block FCC digital discrimination rules. Mixed record.

evidence.title: Press release: Joyce, Rice and Norman introduce the PROMISE Act on social media content moderation
evidence.quote: Unfortunately, we now know that Big Tech and Silicon Valley often do the exact opposite, suppressing speech and views they disagree with.
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants platforms held to their moderation policies through FTC enforcement, a conservative-style targeted rule.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 2481, Romance Scam Prevention Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring dating apps to warn users about banned scammers.

evidence.title: Chairman Joyce opening remarks at Appropriations oversight hearing on the Federal Trade Commission
evidence.quote: Over the last several years, under previous leadership, the FTC routinely strayed from its core mission and stretched the limits of its statutory authorities.
evidence.what_it_shows: Criticizes the Khan-era FTC's aggressive posture and welcomes a narrower agency.

evidence.title: Broadband Breakfast: Joyce's FY27 Financial Services bill would bar FCC funds for enforcing digital discrimination rules
evidence.quote: the subcommittee's legislation would prevent any FCC funds from going toward the enforcement of digital discrimination rules enacted during the Biden administration
evidence.what_it_shows: Uses the spending bill to roll back a Biden-era telecom regulation and trims FCC funding below its request.

preemption.summary: No statement found on whether Washington should override state AI laws. He voted for the May 2025 reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year moratorium, but that vote covered the whole package and is not treated as a position here.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1 (reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year state AI law moratorium)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported the package that included the moratorium; the vote alone does not show his view on preemption.

china_chips.summary: Joyce is a China hawk on education (his CLASS Act banning CCP money in K-12 schools passed the House) and signed the 2022 Ohio GOP letter to fund the CHIPS Act for Intel. No position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China.

evidence.title: Press release: Joyce Applauds House Passage of the CLASS Act blocking CCP influence in classrooms
evidence.quote: The CCP's attempts to shape narratives in our classrooms threaten the fairness and independence of American education
evidence.what_it_shows: General China-hawk posture, but not about chips or export controls.

evidence.title: Ohio Republican letter to congressional leaders urging full funding of the CHIPS for America Act (Joyce listed as signer in Carey release)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported domestic chip manufacturing subsidies for Intel's Ohio plant.

signature: Appropriations chairman who funds the FTC and FCC; wants common-sense guardrails that do not stifle innovation, with targeted bills on deepfake porn and dating-app scams; no data center statements found.

notable_quote.text: While regulators have a responsibility to maintain common-sense guardrails, they should do so in a way that does not stifle innovation and force good-paying jobs overseas

groups: Chairman, House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government
search_notes: Ran about 14 Google News searches (AI under both Dave Joyce and David Joyce, data centers, electricity, deepfakes/DEFIANCE, Big Tech/privacy/scams, China chips/Nvidia, preemption, Take It Down/KOSA, Intel/CHIPS, FSGG chairmanship, Homeland AI). Site listings of joyce.house.gov and appropriations.house.gov; read the PROMISE Act, CLASS Act and China op-ed posts, News-Herald profiles, Broadband Breakfast, and five Appropriations remarks/press pages (FY26 and FY27 FSGG markups, FTC, FCC oversight). Verified votes h145/h279/h347. IMPORTANT: the state context leads placing him in the Energy and Commerce Republican privacy working group as E&C Vice Chairman, and the Guthrie/Joyce/Latta letter on foreign influence in data center opposition, refer to Rep. John Joyce (PA-13), not Dave Joyce (OH-14); those were excluded. The March 2025 Ohio Capital Journal and News 5 Cleveland stories on GOP reactions to repealing the CHIPS Act were blocked, so his 2025 CHIPS stance is unverified.

name: Mike Carey

data_centers.summary: Carey represents the central Ohio data center hub and has voted for Republican bills to add power plants; at a county meeting he described data centers as a source of rising demand to be met with more generation, including solar. He has not publicly addressed ratepayer complaints even as his Democratic challenger campaigns against data center expansion.

evidence.title: Record Herald: Rep. Carey discusses energy demands with Fayette County commissioners
evidence.what_it_shows: Per the paper's account, he framed data centers as a driver of rising electricity demand and said solar can be permitted fastest to add grid supply; no cost concerns were reported.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1047, GRID Power Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported fast-tracking dispatchable power plants that the Ohio sponsor tied to central Ohio data center growth.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 3616, Reliable Power Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported a second Republican grid bill framed around rising power demand.

evidence.title: Spectrum News: Democrat Don Leonard's challenge to Carey centers on stopping data center expansion
evidence.quote: Leonard says his platform is centered on expanding access to healthcare, tackling access to housing and stopping the expansion of data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Data centers are a live campaign issue against him in the 2026 race.

evidence.title: Ohio Capital Journal: constituents rally against Carey over SNAP, Medicaid cuts and his support for data centers
evidence.quote: We are calling on him to restore funding to the critical services like Medicaid, SNAP, fully fund the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act and end all funding to ICE, war, and his support to data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: Activists characterize him as a data center supporter; his office did not respond to the paper's request for comment.

ai_risk.summary: Carey cosponsors the DEFIANCE Act letting victims of AI sexual deepfakes sue, and a bill letting investigators use face-matching to identify abused children. His only AI hearing remarks found were questions about how House offices use ChatGPT. No broader AI safety position found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a civil right to sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes, a targeted guardrail.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6998, Renewed Hope Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting investigators use facial recognition to identify child abuse victims, a pro-use of AI for law enforcement.

evidence.title: Committee on House Administration hearing on AI innovation within the legislative branch (Carey question)
evidence.quote: Along the CAO's ChatGPT working group what has been the most common popular office use? And what do you think some of the biggest shortcomings are?
evidence.what_it_shows: Engaged with AI as a productivity tool for Congress, not as a regulatory question.

tech_regulation.summary: Carey's tech record is about China-linked technology: he cosponsored a 2023 bill banning TikTok on college networks and the 2026 Connected Vehicle Security Act. No statements found on Section 230, antitrust, privacy law or kids' online safety.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 231 (118th), Terminate TikTok on Campus Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported requiring federally funded colleges to ban TikTok on their networks.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car technology from companies tied to China and other adversaries.

preemption.summary: No statement found on whether Washington should override state AI laws. He voted for the May 2025 reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year moratorium, but that vote covered the whole package and is not treated as a position here.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1 (reconciliation bill that carried the 10-year state AI law moratorium)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported the package that included the moratorium; the vote alone does not show his view on preemption.

china_chips.summary: Carey champions building chips in America: he pushed to fund the CHIPS Act for Intel's plant near his district in 2022 and cosponsors the BASIC Act extending the chip factory tax credit. No position found on export controls or Nvidia chip sales to China.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Mike Carey Applauds Historic Intel Investment
evidence.quote: We can no longer afford to rely on foreign countries to produce this technology
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports domestic semiconductor manufacturing as a supply-chain and security issue.

evidence.title: Ohio Republican letter to congressional leaders urging full funding of the CHIPS for America Act (Carey signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined the Balderson-led push to fund chip manufacturing incentives.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3204, BASIC Act (chip manufacturing tax credit extension)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports extending the tax break for chip factories and adding chip design; not an export-control stance.

signature: Central Ohio Republican in the New Albany data center hub who voted for grid-expansion bills and championed Intel's chip plant; no public AI regulation stance found beyond cosponsoring the DEFIANCE Act.

notable_quote.text: We can no longer afford to rely on foreign countries to produce this technology

search_notes: Ran about 15 Google News searches (AI, data centers, electricity bills, deepfakes/chatbots, Big Tech/TikTok, China chips/Intel, preemption, Leonard challenger, House Administration AI, Ways and Means AI, ratepayer pledge, NBC4/Dispatch/OCJ data center coverage). Site listing of carey.house.gov; read the 2022 Intel and CHIPS releases, the CHA AI hearing takeaways, Record Herald, Spectrum News, Springfield News-Sun and the Ohio Capital Journal rally story (via Wayback). Verified votes h145/h279/h347. Cleveland.com's Aug. 23-24, 2026 story on Ohio data center anger and Republicans, Politico's Aug. 2025 and Sept. 2026 data center pieces, the Columbus Dispatch profiles and Spectrum's OH-15 race breakdown were all blocked (403) with no Wayback copy, so any Carey quotes in them are unverified. No statement in his own words on ratepayer costs, AI regulation or preemption was found.
